subject.title: RFC: Skill routing metadata and evaluation hints for Harness-style OpenClaw setups

question: Should ClawHub standardize publisher-supplied routing, risk, and verification declarations only as advisory registry metadata, with no execution or security-enforcement meaning?
rationale: The schema shape, public API representation, ranking use, and boundary between author claims and ClawHub-owned trust evidence determine user safety and long-term compatibility; source inspection cannot choose that contract safely.

options.title: Adopt an advisory v1
options.body: Define a small optional, versioned vocabulary for candidate discovery and verification hints, explicitly separating publisher claims from scanner and moderation evidence.

options.title: Limit v1 to discovery
options.body: Standardize intents and negative applicability first, deferring risk and verification fields until their trust semantics and consumers are proven.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Keep current descriptive metadata and revisit this once Claws discovery and recommendation work identifies a concrete shared consumer.

recommendation.title: Adopt an advisory v1
recommendation.body: Define a small optional, versioned vocabulary for candidate discovery and verification hints, explicitly separating publisher claims from scanner and moderation evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent VISION.md work most directly establishes ClawHub’s discovery, trust, and runtime-execution boundary.
